- When sentiment is consistently negative or near-zero over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–7 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — adjust downward by 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- When sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of downward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — reduce first 5 days’ forecast by 1–3% relative to historical mean.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model may misread sentiment — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
